# V12 selected Amin: complete recorded trajectories

After root confirmed all12 selected games complete, the four Amin games show a regression: frozen V10 wins both cases1/2 at1033; V12 loses both at635. These are opposite seat/spawn-label cases on one consumed83000 placement, not independent maps. Both policies' paired mirrors have exactly equal role-relative public wires, raw/applied actions, validity, original19-field memory and telemetry. All3,336 candidate frames were checked; no new inference, engine replay or games were performed for this report.

| Policy | Case | Result / turns | Candidate invalid / malformed | Original Amin invalid / malformed |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| V10 | 1 | win /1033 |0/0|58/0|
| V10 | 2 | win /1033 |0/0|58/0|
| V12 | 1 | loss /635 |0/0|12/0|
| V12 | 2 | loss /635 |0/0|12/0|

The original opponent's140 invalid actions were retained and normalized by the frozen arena. These are not runtime/deadline faults. Each V12 case's invalid turns are77,103,106,149,152,227,230,263,317,432,435,578; none occurs during the terminal visible wave616–634. Complete control invalid lists remain in the machine report. Synchronous strategy evaluation does not qualify official deployment deadlines, and candidate timing includes recording IO.

## What the guard actually changed

Per V12 game, the guard is active on424/635 frames and rejects/replaces the parent only twice, at249 and495. Each rejection tries one distinct eligible alternative, ranks2 and0 respectively; total probes2, exhausted searches0, guard-induced PASS0. The12 actual PASS actions are the unchanged opening turns0–7,10,11,14,15. V12 builds once at411; neither replacement is a build. This is not repeated search exhaustion, a PASS loop or invalid-action failure.

First candidate raw/applied divergence is249; first differing public observations are250; first opponent raw/applied divergence is283. At249 the exact incoming public wire,19-field memory and key still match the V10 control. The control issues (8,15)→(8,14), moving from army12; V12 instead moves army3 at(12,2) north to neutral(11,2). Recorded guard deficits are13 before,21 after the rejected proposal and13 after the issued alternative. The army at(8,15) remains, then the actual V12 policy moves it left at260 with army13. The alternative supplies a real neutral capture, not a PASS. The common-input control telemetry confirms this was an ordinary campaign transfer: no commitment start/continuation/hold, intercept override, offense start/continuation/override, or pursuit issuance was active. It was not a claimed interception certificate. In the actual control, destination(8,14) was already owned with1 and has13 at250 after transfer/growth; it remains13 through254 while another packet moves. That establishes the transfer outcome, not a later counterfactual rescue.

At495, guard deficits are10 before,11 after the rejected proposal and10 after the alternative. V12 moves army8 at(12,3) north to neutral(11,3). The parent telemetry reports a newly started defender commitment, but this is **unissued**: the guard replaces the action and clears returned defense/offense memory. The exact rejected parent raw action is not generically recorded; this report does not invent it from later V10 history or claim parent action replay. A new collection starts496, continues497, and a defender starts498 at(10,13), continues499 to(8,13), then releases on observable inconsistency500. That incoming wave is survived; it is not the terminal attack.

The early productive concentration at129/142 remains in the identical prefix. Two action substitutions and their memory consequences cause a different adaptive trajectory, but the records do not isolate which substitution or downstream decision caused the eventual loss. No generic proposal-action parity beyond the first common-input control comparison is claimed.

## Complete trajectory and terminal mechanism

The candidate is not uniformly behind economically. At300 V12 has land83–76 and army298–259; at400 land83–97 but army380–354; at600 land118–101 and army528–442. At625 it still leads land121–98 and army515–417. Nevertheless the force needed at home is dispersed.

A large enemy stack is publicly visible at(7,1) with177 at616, later at(7,7) with177 at622 and(6,7) with173 at623. It is not visible at624. At625 a172 stack appears at(6,9), then175 at(7,9),159 at(7,10),157 at(7,11),155 at(8,11), and advances east to139 at(8,16) at634. It captures the general at635 against home54. This is ordinary combat, before deathtouch800. The own15 at(7,10) is consumed as the enemy advances; other nearby owned stacks are much smaller than the invader. At634 aggregate ownarmy491 still exceeds opponent388, which does not prevent the local capture.

The guard is active throughout625–634 and issues the parent's remote moves on every one of those frames. Its recorded before/parent-after/issued-after deficit is identical on each frame:97 at625,99 at626,89 at627–628,86 at629 and84 at630–634. Thus the rule accepts actions that do not worsen an **already positive** projected deficit; it does not force the deficit to be repaired. The candidate continues a remote collection/deployment on the left/lower board and then moves a37–38 packet around columns2–4. The parent has no feasible interception certificate during625–634 and no active defender commitment then. There is no late guard replacement, held-defender loop or fallback-PASS stall to explain this particular terminal failure.

This supports a precise limitation of the tested invariant: preserving current route resistance is insufficient once an overwhelming route is already exposed. It does not prove a legal rescue existed at625 or establish that a stronger mandatory-defense rule would preserve offense or win. The first rejection also shows that a non-worsening alternative can be strategically remote. One bounded next hypothesis is to apply the check only to actually claimed defensive interventions, rather than ordinary campaign transfers like249. This is not proven beneficial:495 does carry an unissued defender-start claim and is still rejected. Separately distinguish prevention of avoidable lost route resistance from repair of an already unsafe route, using actual feasible timing/force and full-game preservation controls rather than treating a one-step invariant as a strength guarantee.

## Evidence and limits

`analysis.json` retains all four results, exact mirror and first-divergence checks, all invalid-turn lists, full original replacement telemetry/memory, correct scalar probe totals and input SHA bindings. `timeline.jsonl` reduces every3,336 recorded candidate frame with economy, actual movement, visible large enemy stacks, defender state and guard deficits. The original full wires, memory and action keys remain in `results/`. `postchecks.json` validates full historical V10 controls including original memory/key/telemetry equality. All frozen sources/helpers/prerequisites were checked before and after reduction. No failed analysis attempt, source change, policy inference or new match occurred. The parent-proposal flags in the timeline remain explicitly labeled proposals and must be masked by `route_guard_parent_action_issued` before attribution to issued behavior.

This selected result fails Amin preservation. It makes no promotion/default change, broad dominance claim, or fresh-map claim.

No policy source changed and no game ran. Projected observations below are passed only to cost calculations, never to either policy.

## Precise release cause

At859 the arrived screen at(8,16) has50. All memory-validity checks pass, required=0, priority=false and keep=true. Its route through the held target costs68 against enemy40 at(7,13), while a longer global minimum route already costs20. A held screen therefore does not represent coverage of every route.

At860 the same screen has61. Arrival, ownership, continuity-of-observation, target legality, remaining visible need and required=0 still pass. The sole validity failure is `timestep > expires`:860>859. Consequently `valid=false`, `keep=false`, and the parent moves the61 to(9,16). This is the configured fixed age limit, not an unexpected execution/memory failure.

At861 there is no incoming defender commitment. The parent builds at(9,16), spending45 from61 and leaving16 before production,17 in the next actual observation. The pure isolated build **does not lower the current cheapest route cost**:21→21, both13edges; the route via old target(8,16) likewise remains26. The money/army expenditure reduces available mobile force, but calling this build the action that opened the global bypass would be unsupported. It also does not prove that forbidding this build would save the episode.

At863 there is no incoming commitment; V5 proposes source18 at(10,16) toward target(8,16), two owned steps. Its accepted certificate reports additional defense17 versus required14 and predicted arrival18. At864 the incoming defender at(9,16) is owned with19, meets its expected18, and all valid/target/time predicates pass. It is one step from target, and `extra=18 >= required14`, so V6 continues up.

At865 the defender has actually reached(8,16) with19. Every validity component passes: prior active, target nonnegative, owned source/target, non-general donor, army>1, army>=expected19, no observation gap, not expired. Visible need remains, target is on a geometric shortest route, target_allowed=true, and there is no winning/adjacent/guard priority. However, required=5: enemy-to-target cost34 plus target-home cost1 equals35, below40. `arrived & required<=0` is false; `progressing` is false because remaining distance is0. Hence `keep_before_priority=false` and `keep=false`. `planned_defense=false` also makes the reversal blocker inapplicable, and the inherited action moves the army back down.

The identical pattern recurs at869(required6),873(required4),877(required2). These are not expiry or arrival-inconsistency releases. The complete scalar table and every inner progression predicate are retained in `predicates.jsonl`; arrays for current/without-defender costs, corridor, owned route distances/extra/arrival/deadline and visible need are in `predicate-fields.npz`. Inactive-memory fields are clipped sentinel calculations, not actual plans; `summary.json` marks their target/validity values null where appropriate.

## Additive donation certificate fails after its own transfers

On the exact863 public board, with enemy40 unchanged, apply only the issued owned transfers (10,16)→(9,16)→(8,16), excluding enemy actions and growth:

| Static stage | Cheapest enemy-home cost | Edges of minimizing route | Cost via selected target |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|Before|26|7|26|
|After first transfer|20|13|26|
|After both transfers|19|13|35|

The pre-transfer17 additional-defense credit is not an actual17 improvement to home-route cost:26+17 would be43, but after both moves the target route costs35 and the cheapest alternative costs19. Vacating the donor at(10,16) enables the south detour through(11,16)→(10,16)→(9,16)→(9,17). The selected donor was outside the original minimum-cost corridor, yet its stationary army constrained an alternate route. The additive credit fails to account for that route becoming cheaper when the donor leaves. Root's independent public-wire Dijkstra produces the same26→20→19 figures; the JAX cost projections and independent paths are bound in the summary.

Actual865 global cost18 differs from the isolated static19 because the real intervening opponent action/growth also occurred. Its target-through cost35 still falls short by5. The release is consistent with a failed pre-arrival certificate, not evidence that the `required<=0` arrived check should simply be bypassed.

Timing caveat: the cheapest post-transfer detour is13edges, versus a7edge geometric enemy-home ETA and6edge enemy-target ETA. Static all-route costs and shortest geometric arrival times describe different routes. This is evidence against the additive feasibility guarantee, not proof that no adaptive interception can work while an opponent detours. The frozen policy also treats ordinary unknown fog cells as traversable; these are its public-terrain estimates, not hidden map revelations.

## Fixtures and next discrimination

`turn860-fixture.json`, `turn861-fixture.json`, and `turn865-fixture.json` contain the exact public-wire path/hash, original action key,19 incoming memory leaves, expected V11/V6 actions and original frame binding. These states belong to the measured V11 trajectory; they are not claims that changing frozen V10 would produce them.

Before editing, separate two hypotheses: a path-specific post-donation certificate that rejects a claimed sufficient route when its own departures invalidate it; and resource allocation when an expiring screen is subsequently spent on a castle. The second is not established by a cheapest-path loss at861, because there is none. Any correction needs a productive fallback and must respect time available on alternate routes. It should preserve the independently supplied controls under `defense-negative-controls/`: a productive rear build, a captured-defender release, and an off-path screen relocated into home while a real threat remains. Forcing every expired/arrived screen to stay would suppress legitimate defenses and could recreate economic stalls.
